question:
Let $A=\begin{bmatrix}k & 2\\3 & k-1\end{bmatrix}$.

(a) Determine all values of $k$ for which $|A|=4$.

(b) For each value of $k$ obtained, evaluate the determinant $\begin{vmatrix}k+1 & 2\\3 & k\end{vmatrix}$.

(c) Examine whether the two determinants obtained in part (b) have the same sign.
explanation:
(a)
Given that $|A|=4$,
$$\begin{vmatrix}k & 2\\3 & k-1\end{vmatrix}=4$$
$$k(k-1)-6=4$$
$$k^2-k-10=0$$
Therefore,
$$k=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{41}}{2}$$

(b)
Let
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}k+1 & 2\\3 & k\end{vmatrix}=k(k+1)-6=k^2+k-6$$
From part (a), $k^2-k-10=0$, so $k^2=k+10$. Hence,
$$D=(k+10)+k-6=2k+4$$
For $k=\frac{1+\sqrt{41}}{2}$,
$$D=2\left(\frac{1+\sqrt{41}}{2}\right)+4=5+\sqrt{41}$$
For $k=\frac{1-\sqrt{41}}{2}$,
$$D=2\left(\frac{1-\sqrt{41}}{2}\right)+4=5-\sqrt{41}$$

(c)
Since $\sqrt{41}>5$,
$$5+\sqrt{41}>0\quad\text{and}\quad5-\sqrt{41}<0$$
Thus, the two determinants have opposite signs.

options.A:
(a) $k=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{41}}{2}$
(b) The determinants are $3+\sqrt{41}$ and $3-\sqrt{41}$
(c) They have opposite signs
options.B:
(a) $k=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{41}}{2}$
(b) The determinants are $5+\sqrt{41}$ and $5-\sqrt{41}$
(c) They have opposite signs
options.C:
(a) $k=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{41}}{2}$
(b) The determinants are $5+\sqrt{41}$ and $5-\sqrt{41}$
(c) Both determinants are positive
options.D:
(a) $k=\frac{1\pm\sqrt{33}}{2}$
(b) The determinants are $5+\sqrt{33}$ and $5-\sqrt{33}$
(c) They have the same sign
